newsitem.title: PERU: Peru to try Tupac Amaru rebel spokesman - agency.
newsitem.headline: Peru to try Tupac Amaru rebel spokesman - agency.

text.p: Peru plans to try for treason the international spokesman of the Marxist guerrilla group that seized the Japanese ambassador's residence, the state news agency Andina reported on Wednesday.
It said the spokesman for the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA), Isaac Velazco, who is based in Germany, will be tried in his absence.

"The terrorist criminal Isaac Cecilio Velazco Fuertes, member of the MRTA, who carries out proselytism in Europe in favour of the extremist group and incites acts of violence in Peru, will face a penal accusation for the crime of betrayal of the fatherland," Andina said.
The MRTA held 72 VIPs hostage for four months inside the Japanese diplomatic residence. Peruvian troops stormed the house on April 22, killing all 14 rebels and freeing all but one hostage alive.
Velazco, a Peruvian granted political asylum in Germany in 1993, won international prominence during the crisis as the MRTA's main mouthpiece.

Since the hostage drama ended, Velazco has infuriated the Peruvian government with accusations that two of the 14 rebels had been summarily executed and warnings that the group will carry out reprisal attacks.

Peru's Interior Ministry has authorised the public prosecutor to bring charges against Velazco before Peru's military court, Andina added. Treason is the maximum crime in Peru's anti-terrorism legislation and carries a life sentence.
Peru's Foreign Ministry has also asked Germany to revoke Velazco's asylum status.
Velazco has said he carries a blue German passport issued by the United Nations as he is a political exile from Peru.
